prior.reason: No source with the route's length, grade, approach or descent exists beyond a one-line Mountain Project mention of a Burdo north-face climb. Local research only links Persis-Index traverse and snowshoe reports, which are a different side of the peak.

The only opened Mount Seattle ascent (trailcatjim 2015) is from Seattle Meadows camp at 4,550 ft on the Skyline loop via the west slope and south ridge (2.3 h up, 1.9 h down), not the Noyes Basin route or the row's Elwha / Low Divide approach. No second source.

Opened Sefrit reports (onehikeaweek 2025 SE ridge, 10.5 mi; turns-all-year S/SW face ski, ~6 h up) both approach from the Nooksack Cirque side and don't mention the Bloody Head Couloir. Route-specific sources (SummitPost, CascadeClimbers) return 403.

No opened source describes the West Slope - East Arete line from the Himmelhorn notch. Abegg's 2009 Twin Needles report reached West Twin from Eye Col (class 3-4, about 5.6 near the top), and Jens Holsten's Pickets traverse blog only mentions bagging the west summit. Search snippets mention a 1969 AAJ note of an easy walk from the Mustard Glacier side; not opened.

Only one route-specific source: the 1958 AAJ note (Beckey and Watson approached via Horse Heaven, camped at a double lakelet below the northwest amphitheater, climbed a gully-flanked line mostly unroped with one chockstone crux, and descended the same way). It gives no times or figures. Climber Kyle and Yellowleaf cover only the standard south-side scramble from Snowy Lakes.

No route source could be opened: the skisickness 2011 NE Arete report returns 404 at both URLs, and the OpenBeta mirror also returned 404. Search snippets confirm the 1979 Skoog-Walseth FA (5.8, loose, per Beckey) and a roughly 3.5 h Swamp Creek approach to Snowy Lakes, but no opened page covers the arete.

Only the 1988 AAJ first-ascent account (Johnson) describes this route: about 6 h from the trailhead past Willow Lake to a 6,200 ft saddle bivy, then III 5.6 loose rock. It says nothing about the descent or exit. WTA's Willow Lake Trail page covers only the trail (23.5 mi one-way from East Bank) and does not mention the climb, so there is no second source for the climb, descent or exit.

Mountain Project gives the 4 pitches and the 60 m rappel from the top of P3, and Abegg gives the shared east-face approach time (37 min-1 h). Neither source, nor the row, gives a base or high-point elevation, distance or day length, so no day figure (hours/miles/gain) can be sourced. The route also usually ends without reaching the summit.

The trip reports found are for the 2007 'Northwest Arayete' (III 5.9, about 1,300 ft, reached from the White Salmon Glacier, 16 h car-to-car on the FA). That is a different line from this row's long Northwest Arete (5.7, AI2+, bushwhack from the White Salmon lodge). No reachable source describes the Arete's days or camps, and the CascadeClimbers reports return 403.
The row has no grade or description, and the name could be either the standard south-side scramble or a technical face route. No source was found that ties a route by this name to the row.
No source describes a West Ridge route on Snoqualmie Mountain, and the row has no grade or description.

Search snippets say only that a North Face route exists (FA 1978, Emerson and Grove) and that Park Creek camp is used for Storm King's standard route. No opened source describes this line's timing or camps.

The only route description is a 2004 CascadeClimbers report (5.4, thin ridge, small nuts, single-rope rappel), and that site returns 403. Mountain Project's 'The Incisor' page is a different peak, in Montana's Crazy Mountains. The climb itself has no source that could be opened.

The opened sources (Belitz, climberkyle) describe only the South Face and the shared Alpental to Pineapple Pass approach (about 3 h, 7 to 10 am, in Belitz). Nothing describes the North Ridge, and the row has no gain, distance or high point, so a day figure cannot be sourced. This replaces the earlier low-confidence plan.
No trip report or route page for the West Face of South Peak in the Gunsight Range could be found or opened. Day counts and timing would be invented.

Only the sverdina log (opened) describes this ridge: a short approach to the Whistler-Cutthroat saddle, an airy crest, and descent by the SW gully, with no times, distance or gain. The Mountain Project 'North Ridge' page that turned up is for Cutthroat Peak, not Whistler, and SummitPost and Mountaineers return 403.
